narration_timeline.text: Why does this Eurasian red squirrel suddenly stop while moving around a tree?
narration_timeline.scene: Red squirrel visible on tree bark.

narration_timeline.text: In a park, trunks and paths create routes between cover and exposed ground.
narration_timeline.scene: Red squirrel in a park near a path.

narration_timeline.text: It climbs, pauses, and crosses open patches, choosing between trees and nearby cover as it moves.
narration_timeline.scene: Two authentic squirrel videos: on a log and moving near a tree.

narration_timeline.text: During a pause, it may settle down to eat, holding food close with its front paws.
narration_timeline.scene: Squirrel visibly holding food against a tree, not assumed to be scanning.

narration_timeline.text: The bushy tail is easy to spot, even when the animal briefly stops moving.
narration_timeline.scene: Separate squirrel video; tail visible, action to be verified.

narration_timeline.text: Its stop-and-go path carries it across the park, rather than one long, straight sprint.
narration_timeline.scene: Squirrel on grass and then on path, two distinct sources.
